newsitem.title: USA: Asarco sees copper stock drawdown this fall.
newsitem.headline: Asarco sees copper stock drawdown this fall.

text.p: Asarco Inc expects renewed copper demand this fall will draw down temporary copper inventory increases accumulated during the summer, chief executive Richard Osborne said Monday.
Telling the company's quarterly analysts' meeting Asarco remains positive on the outlook for the copper market, he said expects its price to remain volatile during the rest of the year.
Noting there is currently about 1.2 weeks of copper supply held in LME and COMEX warehouses, he said the total can be expected to grow during "the normal summer doldrums."

A robust economy in the United States and continued growth in copper consumption in Asia, especially China, have maintained strong copper supply and demand fundamentals thus far this year, Osborne explained.
The Asarco official also restated his view that there will be a world copper supply deficit this year following last year's 172,000 short ton deficity.
But, the company has shifted some of this year's previously expected deficit out to 1998.
In late April Osborne projected a deficit of 53,000 tons in 1997 amd 149,000 tons in 1998.
Today, he put this year's shortfall at 34,000 tons and projected a 173,000 ton world supply deficit for next year.
